# Arsenal - The Swiss App for Gun Collectors (Full Reference)

This is the exhaustive companion to llms.txt. It contains the complete, unabridged content of Arsenal's Home, Details, and FAQ pages, including the full caliber list, full per-collection attribute lists, and full FAQ text. Use llms.txt for a fast overview; use this file to answer specific, granular questions without needing to fetch additional pages.

Official domain: https://arsenal-app.ch/en/
App Store (iOS): https://apps.apple.com/app/arsenal-armamentarium/id6670214648
Google Play (Android): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.m00gendai.arsenal

App name by locale: Arsenal Gun Collection (EN) / Arsenal Waffen & Sammlung (DE) / Arsenal Collection d'Armes (FR) / Arsenal Collezione d'Armi (IT). Interface fully localized into English, German, French, Italian, and Rumantsch Grischun.

Rating: 5/5 stars from 23 ratings (Apple App Store).

---

## HOME PAGE CONTENT

Arsenal is the firearm inventory and gun collection manager for serious collectors, made in Switzerland. Track your guns, ammo stock, and accessories - fully offline, one-time purchase (only 5 CHF), no subscription.

Create a wide variety of collections, with photos and many parameters:
- Firearms
- Ammunition
- Suppressors
- Optics
- Scopes
- Lights & Lasers
- Magazines
- Miscellaneous Accessories
- Conversion Kits
- Barrels
- Books
- Reloading Components
- and new collections are added continuously!

Each entry has a history, so every change can be tracked at any time. You can also record sales. Consumable items (ammunition, powder, bullets, etc.) additionally include a cost overview.

Smart tools:
- QuickShot for quickly logging round counts, linked to your ammunition inventory
- QuickStock for easy management of consumables such as ammunition, powder, bullets, and more, including cost tracking
- QuickMount to conveniently assign accessories and parts to a firearm or another accessory or part

PDF exports are easy to generate too. Choose between predefined lists or create your own with exactly the attributes you need - for example for insurance purposes. CSV export/import is also integrated, as well as full database backup as a ZIP file including all images.

Already using QR codes on your firearms? Integrate them seamlessly into the app and scan directly to the desired item. Not using QR labels yet? Create them right inside the app - using a wide range of predefined label formats (Avery) or define your own.

Additional features: stock warnings, cleaning interval reminders, keyword filters, search and sort functions, autocomplete, multiple views and color themes (light and dark), freely selectable units of measurement, and more.

Everything is 100% offline - no internet connection required. All data is stored locally on your device and can be exported at any time. No servers, no telemetry.

Available in five languages: German, French, Italian, English and Rumantsch Grischun.

Developed in Switzerland, primarily tailored to the needs of Swiss firearms collectors. International users can select their country (e.g. the USA), and the app automatically adapts by displaying country-specific firearm categories.

One-time purchase, use forever, updates for as long as the app exists. No subscriptions, no in-app purchases, no ads!

## DETAILS PAGE — ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONALITY (FULL TEXT)

**QuickShot - Keep track of how many rounds went through your gun**
QuickShot is a "rangelog light" and allows to log shots taken with a firearm directly from the collection overview. It is connected to the ammunition in the app, meaning QuickShot detects if you have caliber-compatible ammunition in stock. This allows you to not only quickly log a shooting session, but also directly subtract the spent rounds from your ammunition stock. You can also just log shots without touching your ammunition stock. Using QuickShot will update the used firearm with shots fired and date of last shooting, and the ammunition, if applicable.

**QuickStock - Keep track of your consumables' stock increase and decrease**
QuickStock is a smart utility to quickly top up your consumables (ammunition, bullets, casings, primers, powder) directly from the collection overview. You can quickly log increase and decrease of stock, and also add how much you paid for your top-up. In the detail view of your consumables, you will find a "costs" tab, which lists all top-ups, how much you paid, and what the average price is. For powder, you can specify the quantity unit, so you can log a decrease in grains despite having the powder amount unit set to pounds, for example.

**QuickMount - Keep track of where your accessories or weapon parts are mounted to**
QuickMount allows you to quickly "mount" an accessory or a weapon part to a gun, another accessory, or another weapon part. This way, you always know where an accessory is mounted, or which weapon has which accessories attached. A convenient, categorized list (with images) makes it easy to quickly select your target gun, accessory, or weapon part. In the tile view, icons at the bottom show the type of accessory or weapon part mounted; the detail view's "accessories" tab lets you unmount or remount; the tile view top shows what a part/accessory is currently mounted on.

**QR Code Integration & Creation**
QR Codes are a quick and easy way to physically track your inventory. If you already employ QR Codes (e.g. tags on guns or stickers on ammo boxes), simply scan the existing code when creating a new collection entry to link it. Use the scan button in the collection overview to scan a code and immediately display the linked item, no matter where you are in the app. If you don't have QR codes yet but want them, Arsenal features a complete customizable QR Code Label generator: select the collection, the items (or all of them), which attributes appear on the label (or none, for just the code), and the format — Arsenal generates a print-ready PDF. Several predefined formats are included (most commonly Avery/Zweckform) in DIN A4 or US Letter, or you can create and save your own custom format. QR codes can also be left off entirely if you just want plain labels.

**Database Import/Export**
Arsenal uses SQLite under the hood. Export formats:
- Full Database Export: a zipped folder with the raw SQLite database and a folder with all images. This is the standard backup format and the one to use when switching devices.
- CSV Export: a CSV file of the specified collection, useful for physical printouts or editing on a computer. Does not include images, only references to their on-device location — reimporting the CSV (without deleting app data) re-links images correctly.

Import formats:
- Full Database Import: imports the zipped database + images folder; requires the naming convention/format set automatically by the export.
- Arsenal CSV Import: imports a file generated by Arsenal's own CSV Export from the same app version.
- Custom CSV Import: imports any CSV, with manual column-to-database field mapping via an in-app helper dialog. Use this to migrate from a third-party app, a spreadsheet, or an older Arsenal CSV version.

Important: the `caliber` field in imported CSVs must match Arsenal's expected caliber notation exactly, or QuickStock functionality and other behavior may be affected.

**PDF Lists**
Two universal PDF lists:
- Complete Gun List (table): Manufacturer, Model Name, Caliber, Serial, Permit reference, Acquisition Date — for insurance, agency requests, or general documentation.
- Custom List: any collection, any chosen attributes (e.g. value without serial for insurance, or just designation and caliber for an ammo list).

Country-specific predefined lists (currently Switzerland):
- Gun List according to WA Article 5 (table): Manufacturer, Model Name, Caliber, Serial, Permit reference, Acquisition Date, Reason why it is under Article 5 — useful for collectors' permit applications or when a weapons bureau requests an excerpt of prohibited items.
- Complete Gun List with WA Article 5 properties: a hybrid list showing the full collection plus Article 5 status/reason, for bureaus wanting a complete list rather than only the Article 5 subset.

Each collection item can also be printed as a "gallery print" showing every image, tags, and all attributes — useful for physical display or as a sales flyer.

**Customizable Units**
Freely choose length/weight units per purpose (e.g. metric throughout except powder, or bullet weight in ounces). A general weight and length unit is also provided for future attributes. You can change units anytime; the database always stores values in milligrams and millimeters internally and converts for display. For powder, it's recommended to use commercial units (kg/g for metric, lb/oz for imperial); stock increase/decrease can each use a different unit (e.g. top up in kilograms, log reloading usage in grains). Any world currency can be set for price fields, but this is cosmetic only — no currency conversion or inflation adjustment is applied, by design, to preserve strict offline operation. Most users use a single currency; if a purchase was made in another currency, enter the converted value. Yearly inflation percentages per country (from 1980 onward) are a planned future feature.

**Item History**
Every change/edit to a collection item is logged: when the change was made, what changed, the old value, and the new value. This provides both a full audit trail and a safety net if you enter an incorrect value and don't recall the original.

**Cost History**
Consumables (Ammunition, Bullets, Cases, Primers, Powder) have a Cost History tab showing purchase date, total amount, total price paid, and average price — useful for monitoring spending and price trends.

**Mark as Sold**
Items can be marked as sold while remaining in the database; you can choose to keep them visible (greyed out) or hide them entirely. When "selling," you can record buyer name, sell date, sell price, permit references, and personal notes. These details cannot be amended afterward, so accuracy at entry time matters. They are displayed above all other attributes when viewing a sold item.

**Tags**
Tags group items within a collection (e.g. tagging books under "Swiss Military Weapons," or classifying weapons by subtype — from a simple rifle/pistol/revolver split to fine-grained categories like toploading revolvers, cap & ball revolvers, magnum revolvers). Any tag scheme can be used; a management dialog tracks existing tags so you don't need to retype them.

## FAQ — FULL TEXT

### Data Privacy and Security

**Does Arsenal require an account?**
No, Arsenal has no user accounts, login or registration.

**Where is the data saved and who has access to it?**
Your collection database is stored locally on your device and only you have access to it.

**Is my data encrypted?**
Yes. Arsenal uses SQLCipher, an open-source database encryption library, to encrypt your data with AES-256. The encryption key is generated on your device and stored in the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore — it never leaves your device.

**What happens if I get a decryption error / my data suddenly becomes unreadable?**
Decryption failures are extremely rare and usually indicate corruption of the encryption key or secure storage. Unfortunately, without the encryption key the database cannot be recovered. Regular backups are therefore strongly recommended.

**What permissions does Arsenal need, and why?**
Arsenal needs permission to access your file system (to import/export your database and select images from your gallery) and to access your camera (to take photos of collection items and scan QR codes).

**Does Arsenal collect analytics?**
No, Arsenal itself does not collect analytics, telemetry, usage statistics or collection data, nor does it transmit your collection to the developer. Google Play and the Apple App Store may collect their own diagnostic, purchase or download information per their own privacy policies — this is outside Arsenal's control and does not include any application data.

### Legal

**Does using Arsenal fulfill or replace any legal record-keeping obligations?**
Arsenal does not replace any official documents, nor is it accredited to function as a legal alternative for existing documents or legal frameworks. It is a personal tool to track your firearm and related collections for personal use. It does, however, provide the possibility to generate collection reports (e.g. gun lists) tailored for specific requirements, such as insurance companies or government agencies.

**Does Arsenal report anything to police or other weapons authorities?**
No. Your collection data stays private, on your device, and only you have access to it. The developer has no access to your collection because it never leaves your device.

### Data Backup, Synchronization & Portability

**What happens if I lose or replace my phone — can I restore my collection?**
The privacy focus and avoidance of network connectivity means there is no cloud backup or server synchronization. It is your responsibility to back up your database regularly via the export options. If you replace your phone, export the database from your old phone and import it on the new one.

**Can I import data from Excel or a competitor app?**
Yes, your own Excel files (in CSV format) can be imported, with field handling configured directly in the app. Calibers must be named exactly as specified in the app or the QuickShot function will not work (see the full caliber list above). Multiple calibers are separated by ", ". Importing as CSV does not support images — these must be added in the app.

### Pricing & Access

**Is Arsenal a one-time purchase or a subscription?**
Arsenal is strictly a one-time purchase. Buy once, use forever, including any future updates.

**What happens to my data if I delete the app or app data?**
Deleting (uninstalling) the app deletes the database as well, so your data is lost if you did not back it up. The same applies when deleting app data via phone settings.

**Is there a free trial or demo version?**
No, Arsenal currently doesn't offer a trial version. Since the app is a one-time purchase, both Google Play and the Apple App Store offer refund options if the app doesn't meet expectations.

### Practical Use

**Which platforms are supported?**
Arsenal is available for both Android and iOS. It requires Android 7.0 or newer, and iOS 15.5 or newer.

**Does Arsenal work offline?**
Yes, Arsenal has been built with strict offline operation in mind and does not require any internet connection to function. The About section contains links to external resources that require internet to display; all collection management features continue to work fully offline.

**Can I use Arsenal on multiple devices?**
Yes. Export your database from one device and import it on another. Arsenal intentionally does not synchronize devices automatically because it does not use cloud services.

**Can I use the PDF exports for insurance documentation or a police-requested inventory list?**
Yes. Arsenal features flexible PDF export generation with predefined and customizable exports tailored to specific needs.

**Can I create custom attributes beyond what's built in?**
No, the attributes are fixed and not extensible, to avoid conflicts with future updates.

**Can I define custom calibers when they're not in the built-in list?**
No, the calibers are fixed and not extensible, to avoid conflicts with future updates and to keep QuickShot/QuickStock functionality in sync (both depend on the correct caliber format). If a caliber is missing, you can request it from the developer and it will be added in the next update. You can bypass this restriction by importing a CSV where caliber entries are not validated, but this is not recommended and can lead to unexpected behavior — back up the database first if attempting this.

**What happens to my collection if I sell a firearm to someone else — is there a transfer/handoff record?**
Yes. Sales can be recorded with sell date, sell price, buyer permit reference, and personal remarks. Sold items remain in the database unless explicitly deleted, but can be hidden via settings.

**What languages does the app support?**
English, German, French, Italian, and Rumantsch Grischun. Changing language is seamless and can be done at any time.

### General

**I already use a competitor app, why should I switch to Arsenal?**
There are several alternative apps, especially on Android, serving the same purpose as Arsenal. However, per the developer: most are US-oriented; they seem to have no language selection or employ auto-translation; they do not seem to have the same range of functions, or if they do, they seem unintuitive and cumbersome; the developer can sometimes be difficult to identify or contact (an LLC in front of the developer) and sometimes appears not to interact with the community; they can cost twice as much, may have non-transparent in-app purchases or advertising, or subscription-based payment models; some seem to not be in active development.

Arsenal, on the other hand: is primarily tailored to Swiss needs but also usable worldwide, offering a choice in displayed units of measurement; is available in five languages, with German and English translated by hand and French, Italian and Rumantsch Grischun via a Swiss translation service; has a modern, simple, and functional user interface; has a private Swiss developer who is actively known in the Swiss weapons and shooting community and interacts with it; costs a one-time fee of 5 CHF for life, including all future updates, with no ads, subscriptions, or in-app purchases; is in constant development.

Ultimately, everyone decides for themselves which app, if any, is best suited — sometimes a spreadsheet is sufficient.

### Support

**Can I see the development progress of the app?**
Yes, the current development status, including planned and requested features, is published on Trello (English only): https://trello.com/b/aewI0VKW/arsenal

**Where can I voice my feedback, critique and wishes?**
Official thread on waffenforum.ch: https://waffenforum.ch/forum/index.php?thread/2883-arsenal-die-schweizer-app-f%C3%BCr-waffensammler/&pageNo=1
Via email: info@mrweber.ch

### AI - Artificial Intelligence

**Does Arsenal send my data to AI services?**
No, Arsenal does not send your data anywhere; it remains strictly on your device.

**Does Arsenal have AI functionality?**
Arsenal does not rely on cloud-based AI services or generative AI. It currently includes on-device QR code recognition, which processes data entirely on-device and transmits nothing externally. Any future intelligent features, such as OCR, will likewise be designed to run entirely on-device without transmitting data.

**Was AI used during development? If so, in what capacity?**
Yes. AI is used as a development aid in much the same way as documentation, technical books, or specialized forums. Arsenal is not generated by AI — the developer has extensive experience with JavaScript, TypeScript and React predating modern AI tools. Every AI-generated suggestion is critically reviewed, tested, and manually adapted before being incorporated into the app.

**Why doesn't Arsenal rely on cloud-based AI?**
Arsenal is designed around privacy, offline operation, and long-term reliability. Cloud-based AI services generally require transmitting data to external providers and incur ongoing operating costs. To remain fully functional offline, independent of third-party AI providers, and available as a one-time purchase without subscriptions or recurring fees, Arsenal intentionally does not rely on cloud-based AI services. On-device technologies, such as QR code recognition and potentially future OCR, are compatible with this philosophy because they process data entirely on-device.
